name: ec-add-identity-right
note: N-104 OPERAND GATE: ecAdd validates q before it adds - exactly 64 bytes (CL-BUG-095) and both coordinates below p (R-117) - and the identity answer q is only ecAdd's answer for a q that passes. The rewrite keeps that validation, ahead of the alias, as plain ANF built only from forms no rule here matches (so the fixed-point tiers cannot rewrite it on a later pass): <b>_px = ecPointX($x); <b>_py = ecPointY($x); <b>_fp = p; <b>_pxok = <b>_px < <b>_fp; <b>_pyok = <b>_py < <b>_fp; <b>_ok = <b>_pxok && <b>_pyok; <b>_gate = assert(<b>_ok), where <b> is the rewritten binding's name. Without it a malformed q was accepted by the default compile and aborted under disableEcOptimizer. ecAdd deliberately does NOT require on-curve (R-157), so neither does this gate. Pinned by packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/n104-ec-optimizer-operand-gate.test.ts (execution, both modes) and each tier's N-104 optimizer test.

name: ec-mul-one
note: N-104 OPERAND GATE: ecMul aborts unless q is on the curve or is the all-zero O (R-157, emitPointGate), and the answer this rule substitutes is only ecMul's answer for such a q. The rewrite keeps that validation, ahead of the rewritten binding, as plain ANF built only from forms no rule here matches: <b>_inf = INFINITY; <b>_isinf = $x === <b>_inf (bytes); <b>_oncurve = ecOnCurve($x); <b>_ok = <b>_isinf || <b>_oncurve; <b>_gate = assert(<b>_ok), where <b> is the rewritten binding's name - the same predicate, in the same order, as emitPointGate. ecOnCurve carries the width and canonicity checks, so this subsumes the ecAdd gate exactly as R-157 does. Pinned by packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/n104-ec-optimizer-operand-gate.test.ts (execution, both modes) and each tier's N-104 optimizer test.

name: ec-add-negate-cancel
note: N-251 GATE (user decision R96): ecNegate($x) has the same x as $x, so the replaced ecAdd doubles exactly when y($x) = 0, and N-110 made the adder ABORT on a doubling with px != 0 and py == 0. The rewrite keeps that abort, ahead of the INFINITY binding, as plain ANF built only from forms no rule here matches: <b>_px = ecPointX($x); <b>_py = ecPointY($x); <b>_zero = 0; <b>_pxz = <b>_px === <b>_zero; <b>_pynz = <b>_py !== <b>_zero; <b>_ok = <b>_pxz || <b>_pynz; <b>_gate = assert(<b>_ok), where <b> is the rewritten binding's name. The px == 0 term is N-110's own exemption: ecNegate(O) = O and O + O = O, so x = O still gives O. Width and canonicity need no gate: the inner ecNegate($x) call checks both and is never dead-code-eliminated. Pinned by packages/runar-testing/src/__tests__/n251-ec-negate-cancel-y0.test.ts (execution, both modes) and each tier's N-251 optimizer test.

name: ec-mul-associative
note: CONSTANT-OPERAND PRECONDITION, as for ec-mulgen-linear: k1 * k2 is folded mod n at rewrite time, so both scalars must resolve to compile-time constants (opOperandsAreConst in compilers/go/frontend/ec_rules_engine.go). Runtime scalars are left alone — an unlock-argument scalar is attacker-chosen and cannot be reduced by the compiler, and firing there is exactly the CL-BUG-017 divergence R-031 closed. This rule and ec-mul-distributive carried "supported": ["ts"] long after Rust, Python, Ruby and Java implemented them; the Go engine is the only tier that reads the tag, so it was the only tier declining the rewrite — a live 5-vs-1 hex divergence on any nested ecMul with constant scalars. Pinned by TestECOptimizer_MulAssociative* in compilers/go/frontend. N-460: "fuses" lists the operand positions holding the inner calls this fusion subsumes; the rule fires only when at least one of them can then be eliminated, so the rewrite never grows the script (FusionScope in packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts, fusionScope in compilers/go/frontend/ec_rules_engine.go).

name: ec-mulgen-linear
note: CONSTANT-OPERAND PRECONDITION: this rewrite fires only when BOTH scalars resolve to compile-time constants; the sum is then folded mod n at rewrite time. Runtime (non-constant) scalars are left alone. That is not an arbitrary limit — it is what makes the seven tiers agree byte-for-byte. All six hand-written tiers (ts, rust, python, zig, ruby, java) guard on getConstInt/get_const_int; the Go engine is data-driven off this file and used to fire the rule unconditionally, emitting a plain bin_op '+' helper for runtime scalars. The script it produced was VALID (emitEcMulGen/emitEcMul reduce the scalar mod n before the ladder — emitScalarReduce in ec-codegen.ts / ecEmitScalarReduce in codegen/ec.go — so an unreduced k1 + k2 never reached the ladder unreduced) but it was a DIFFERENT script from every other tier for the same source, which conformance invariant 2 forbids. The Go guard now lives in opOperandsAreConst (compilers/go/frontend/ec_rules_engine.go). NOTE this means the scalar reduce is no longer load-bearing FOR THIS RULE; it remains load-bearing in its own right because unlock-argument scalars are attacker-chosen and may be >= n or negative (see ec-scalar-domain.test.ts). The k1 + k2 = 0 (mod n) case agrees with the unrewritten spelling only because affineAdd returns the all-zero point for P + (-P); see the P == -Q comment in ec-codegen.ts. Pinned by ec-mulgen-linear-parity.test.ts (TS/Go hex parity for both the runtime and the constant shape) and by TestECOptimizer_MulGenLinearSkipsRuntimeScalars in compilers/go/frontend. N-460: "fuses" lists the operand positions holding the inner calls this fusion subsumes; the rule fires only when at least one of them can then be eliminated, so the rewrite never grows the script (FusionScope in packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts, fusionScope in compilers/go/frontend/ec_rules_engine.go).

name: ec-mul-distributive
note: OPERAND ORDER: ecMul is ecMul(point, scalar) (packages/runar-lang/src/builtins.ts). This rule used to be spelled ecMul($k1, $p) / ecMul($k2, $p), which bound the POINT to $k1/$k2 and unified $p on the SCALAR — so the replace template summed two POINTS into the scalar slot. It was inert only because the rule also carried "supported": ["ts"] and the TS tier never reads this file; dropping that tag without fixing the spelling made the Go engine rewrite ecAdd(ecMul(P, k), ecMul(Q, k)) into ecMul(P + Q, k). Because $p now sits in the point slot, unification gives the same-point precondition the six hand-written tiers spell explicitly (leftVal.args[0] === rightVal.args[0] in anf-ec.ts, _same_binding in anf_optimize.py, and the equivalents in Rust/Ruby/Java). CONSTANT-OPERAND PRECONDITION: as for ec-mulgen-linear, the rewrite fires only when both scalars are compile-time constants so the sum can be folded mod n at rewrite time (opOperandsAreConst in compilers/go/frontend/ec_rules_engine.go). Pinned by TestECOptimizer_MulDistributive* in compilers/go/frontend. N-460: "fuses" lists the operand positions holding the inner calls this fusion subsumes; the rule fires only when at least one of them can then be eliminated, so the rewrite never grows the script (FusionScope in packages/runar-compiler/src/optimizer/anf-ec.ts, fusionScope in compilers/go/frontend/ec_rules_engine.go).
